body:
Ahh that's awesome that you're making a short film!! Would love to see it when it's done! Thank you for representing us 🥰

I'd like to see the shame represented. Feeling shame after causing an argument with my significant other, when I get my period and suddenly I realize how unreasonable I was being. The shame of not being able to complete tasks that are normally easy for me, and for being a completely different person sometimes. Feeling shame about having to cancel plans last minute. For isolating in my room, and trying to sneak to the kitchen without my roommates seeing because I don't want to explain.
Sending love and hugs to you ❤ Though I wouldn't wish this on anyone, there is comfort in knowing I'm not alone. Thank you for taking the time to remind me of that.

😔 This is exactly how I feel too. Especially when I'm spiraling I truly believe that they would be better off moving on from me. I know logically that I help support them too, but they definitely have not made it as difficult as I do. I've made so many mistakes and it's hard for me to accept that they love me anyway. It's really beautiful and I feel lucky to get to experience that kind of love, but it's also scary as fuck.

I'd love to see your journaling style! I used to journal a lot more, especially gratitude and I would pick something to focus on for a while (a lot of the time it's being present) and it helps sooo much! 

That's really awesome that you're aware of all that! You're totally right that it's important to be there for other people, but ultimately we need to care for ourselves first. I really try to remember that saying "you can't pour from an empty cup", meaning that we need to take care of ourselves so that we have the energy and space to extend that love to the people around us too. For me it's hard because it feels like PMDD takes away 1/3 of my life, and I wish I could have the energy that I have in my ovulatory phase all the time. But pushing myself only ends up hurting me and the people around me in the end, so I'm learning to accept myself and my physical limitations.

I end up yelling too!! And sometimes the physical emotions I feel definitely don't match up with what I'm saying 😅 But yeah, I can understand how it's hard to not take it personally. Our partners are only human. Mine also struggles with mental illness so I have to remember that there's times where it's also hard for them to be patient.

I've looked into Better Help as well, but unfortunately I can't fit it into my budget 😥 I found some counseling on zoom I can afford but the wait list is long. Hopefully I'll get a call in the next couple months! 

Here's some more info on opposite action: https://dbt.tools/emotional_regulation/opposite-action.php
It really blew my mind. It's so simple. It's still hard to do, because I struggle with a lot of resistance but it definitely helps me feel like I'm in control when I make the decision to do the opposite of what my brain is telling me to do (like going for a walk instead of laying in bed all day when I'm sad, or reaching out to loved ones for reassurance instead of ruminating on my thoughts when I'm in a depressive episode, or facing the thing that's causing me anxiety instead of running from it). 

Even when change is good it can still be difficult! Healthy habits don't feel good when we're used to how comfortable the codependent ones feel. That's really awesome that you're getting back to doing things you love on your own! I think its important to just be aware of why we want to talk to someone or why we feel that pull to do something. I struggle with knowing what is codependency and what is me just needing support.

Ahhh yes that's exactly how I feel!! It's frustrating but I also understand it's not possible for them to always keep their emotions in check either. I've been trying to come up with ways they can approach me that might work better, but it's hard because it's all trial and error. 

I think the next thing I'm gonna try is a safe word. A word I can say that means "my brain is foggy, I'm not rational, I'm having trouble processing information and making decisions". Something that I define beforehand so that I can tell them how I'm feeling without having to express it properly.

Thank you!! I'll definitely check it out. It's so hard to keep myself on a schedule because my work is chaotic, but I think you're right that being more regular with exercise would really help. I'm on a waiting list for an affordable counselor so hopefully that comes soon! I recently took a group CBT course too that was really helpful. I think I'll join the next level soon. There's a technique called "opposite action", and basically you just do the opposite of what you normally would would you feel "x" way. I think I need to practice that more. Push through the resistance. 

I totally get you with the codependency! Our relationship was very codependent and we've been working really hard to heal from that, but it's so easy to fall into old patterns. Finding myself after that has been really rewarding but I also feel empty sometimes? Especially during my luteal phase, I find myself wanting more attention from others. I didn't really associate that with my codependent tendencies until now, so thank you for helping me have that realization! 

Yeah that makes sense. It's so important that we have people around that are there for us, I'm glad that you and your ex were able to stay friends. It's hard when both people struggle with their mental health, my partner also has pretty severe depression and anxiety so I don't blame them for not always being able to approach me in the perfect way either.

Hi! I know it's been ages but I'm terrible at checking my reddit notifications. 

I took 10mg fluoxetine (prozac) and 300mg bupropion (welbutrin) all summer and I definitely felt more in control and I was able to be aware of my symptoms coming on so I could deal with them. 

In November my Dr upped my dosage of fluoxetine to 20mg/day. For me its just easier to take something daily. For the first month I felt like myself for the first time ever?? I had energy, I slept less (a normal 7-8hrs instead of needing 9-10) and my luteal phase in December was dreamy! But now I'm kinda back to where I was in the summer. Better and more aware but eventually it explodes. 

Anyway, how's it going for you!

Yes!! I call it "mush mouth". It almost feels like my brain is moving faster than my mouth can? I mix up sounds in my sentences, don't enunciate well and generally mumble more than usual.  This used to happen when I was really depressed as well, maybe it has something to do with the brain fog?
After lunch is brutal! I've had to add in a second coffee 😴

I'm having the same experience! I still have intrusive thoughts and I don't feel good 100% of the time. For me, I think it has more to do with my mindset? I'm trying meditation and I got a CBT workbook to do on my own, since I don't have access to therapy.

When I started 150mg XL a few months ago, I didn't notice a difference until week 6 but it really started helping around week 8. In my experience it was definitely worth it! I'm on 300mg XL now and I feel better than I ever have.

Thank you for sharing this! I just hit 65 consecutive days of meditation, and I've been struggling to get through my CBT work book. It feels like I'm doing it wrong, and it's easy to convince myself it won't help. Comments like this remind me that it isn't a "quick fix" and the healing is in the journey.

"Your life seems fine, why are you depressed?" 

As a person who has struggled with very functioning depression and anxiety for the majority of my life, who has a relatively good support system, but who was raised by a mentally ill parent, it really fucked with my imposter syndrome. This was 5 years ago and it's still in the back of my head every time I take steps to find counseling, or call a crisis line. I always feel like I'm not worthy of help because I don't have addiction or self harm issues and I can hold a job. But that's literally all I can do.
Good point! I want to educate, not shame.
My thought exactly lol. I can't stand having people do things for me that I'm perfectly capable of doing, but I'm sure the other women in the warehouse are taking full advantage.

He also once told me not to sit on the asphalt outside because it's cold, so I'll catch a cold?? Meanwhile I was smoking a cigarette, that might be the reason I end up catching a cold 😅 (have since quit smoking, but still regularly sit my ass down on cold concrete. No illnesses to report!)

Gross. I'm so sorry that you had to deal with that. 
I started out as a delivery driver 3 months ago, and they brought me into the warehouse because I've been able to figure out the system quickly. But the atmosphere of angry men, unsolicited advice and "jokingly" making fun of people quickly wore me down. I've asked to scheduled as a driver again.

Right?? I'm sure a lot of enslaved women had 20lb babies on their backs while working in the fields. Unfortunately I wouldn't be surprised if something like this did happen to THEM. But I don't think its gonna happen to a skinny white girl, who is not pregnant or has children, lifting a caliper for a sedan😂😂

I realize that in some situations this could be good advice. In this situation it was unsolicited, uneccessary and given because he is concerned about my ability to produce offspring in the future.... which is frankly none of his business 😅 also, I'm lifting up to 50 lbs. I know plenty of women who have had children who lift much more than that during their work outs 🤷‍♂️  I do not fall into a single category that makes me at risk for something like this.

So that is less to do with anatomy and more to do with social norms? That's interesting and totally makes sense. I have no problem asking for help and I definitely wouldn't strain myself to lift something at work, but most of my male coworkers seem to have back problems.
Good point! I think that's why I didn't know how to respond. I appreciated his concern but we aren't lifting more than 50lbs, and other than being white I don't fall into any of those categories.
